value.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for turning every noticed error, issue, design flaw or annoyance into recorded, fixed and verified work
value.lets_workers: Record every error, issue, design flaw or annoyance anyone notices as a finding with evidence, at once, then reproduce it, fold duplicates together, fix it, have a different worker verify the fix, add a guard shown to fail without the fix, close it through a gate and, when the disclosure rules allow it, prepare a public summary for the owner. Failures stay on the record.
value.notice_rule: Whoever notices a problem records it. A worker that notices one during any other verb, in any pack, returns a proposed record-finding verb with its evidence in proposed_verbs, and an authorized requester enqueues it; a person can claim record-finding directly. Workers create nouns and propose verbs; they never enqueue.

flow.when: As soon as anyone notices a problem, even one that will be fixed a minute later.
When the problem needs to be seen again before a fix; security findings go to the security review pack instead.
After recording: fold duplicates together by fingerprint, then set kind, severity and sensitivity. Rerun it when a reproduction, fix, verification or guard points at the finding.
For a triaged finding; an annoyance or other matter of taste gets two or three options for a person.
For the chosen option: a test fails first, then passes.
By a different worker than the fixer, where the problem was seen.
When the fix has no guard yet, or its guard has not been shown to fail without the fix.
When the close gate can pass; deterministic.
Only when the disclosure rules allow it; the owner decides whether and where it appears.
Periodically, across closed findings, for causes that keep coming back.

rules: Record first. Recording never waits for a fix, a reproduction or a decision.
Failures stay on the record. Nothing is deleted or rewritten to hide a mistake; later steps write new versions or new nouns.
An annoyance is a real finding. When its fix is a matter of taste, a person chooses, never an agent.
The worker who made a fix does not verify it.
A guard counts only after it is shown to fail without the fix and pass with it.
Never publish details of an unfixed security finding.

shape.note: The flow follows the reproduce-then-repair breakdown pattern, with a person's checkpoint for taste calls.

related_packs.use: add-regression-guard proves a guard with its trust rule, and review-checks confirms the verdict.
propose-fix writes a palette brief for an annoyance or other taste call, and the person's choice decides the fix.
A security finding is scoped, reproduced in a local sandbox and fixed through it, and stays private until fixed everywhere.
A documentation finding can be audited and rewritten through it.
A fix too large for one verb becomes a proposed breakdown.

A fix that would build something new, such as a shared tool or check, first surveys what already exists and lays out the alternatives; a repair that restores something to its own tested contract does not need to.

value.title: How every noticed problem becomes nouns and verbs
value.category_reason: A reusable procedure with its guardrails, followed by every verb in this pack.
lifecycle: record-finding writes the finding the moment the problem is noticed.
reproduce shows it happening again, in the smallest way that still fails.
triage folds duplicates together by fingerprint and sets kind, severity and sensitivity.
propose-fix names the cause and one to three options, each with the guard that would show it works.
fix makes the chosen option with a test that fails first.
verify-fix, by a different worker, reruns the reproduction on the unfixed and fixed versions.
add-regression-guard shows a guard failing without the fix and passing with it.
close applies the gate and writes the closing version of the finding.
publish-finding prepares a public summary when the disclosure rules allow it.
review-patterns looks across findings for causes that keep coming back.
rules: Record every noticed error, issue, design flaw or annoyance, even one fixed a minute later. Recording never waits.
Failures stay on the record. Never delete or rewrite a finding to hide a mistake; Tessera keeps every version.
One finding per problem: triage folds duplicates into the oldest finding with the same fingerprint, which keeps all their evidence.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs. They never enqueue; an authorized requester decides which proposals run.
The fixer never verifies their own fix.
A guard is trusted only after it fails without the fix and passes with it, twice, by the checks of checks trust rule.
A matter of taste is decided by a person through a taste palette; silence is never a choice.
Merged is not deployed: a fix merged but not running where the problem was seen leaves the finding fixed_not_deployed.
When a fix needs an authority nobody has given, such as a new spending allowance or a changed limit, record blocked with one question and never work around it.

statuses.open: Recorded; nobody is making a fix yet.
statuses.in_progress: A fix is being proposed or made.
statuses.fixed: A fix is in place where the problem lives.
statuses.fixed_not_deployed: The fix is merged but not running where the problem was seen.
statuses.verified: A different worker confirmed the fix where the problem was seen.
statuses.closed: The close gate passed: verified independently, with a guard shown to fail without the fix or a written waiver.
statuses.duplicate: Folded into an older finding with the same fingerprint, which keeps its evidence.
statuses.wont_fix: A person decided not to fix it, with a reason; it stays on the record.

resolved: A verification by a different worker than the fixer says fix_verified where the problem was seen.
A guard is shown to fail without the fix and pass with it, or a waiver gives the written reason no guard can run.
The closing version passes every record check.
duplicate: The pinned canonical finding lists this finding among its duplicates.
wont_fix: A person's recorded decision is pinned; an agent alone never decides not to fix.

follow_ups: New problems found while fixing or verifying become proposed record-finding verbs, never silent extra changes.
A fixed finding without a trusted guard gets a proposed add-regression-guard verb.
A cause seen in several places gets a proposed review-patterns run.

An option that would build something new, rather than repair something to its own tested contract, gets the prior art and alternatives pack's survey-existing and research-alternatives verbs proposed first.

value.title: The four kinds of finding, how to tell them apart and the fingerprint rule
value.category_reason: A reusable classification guide that every recording and triage verb applies.

error.means: Something gives a wrong result, crashes, leaks or accepts what it should refuse.
error.evidence: A minimal reproduction, a log excerpt or a measurement.
error.usual_fix: A code or configuration change with a test that fails without it.

issue.means: Something is missing, stale, misconfigured or waiting on a person, or a step in a process went wrong, without wrong behavior in the code itself.
issue.evidence: A link, receipt, status code or timestamp; for a process issue, the direction that applied and the action that broke it, with times.
issue.usual_fix: Content, configuration, a person's action or a change to the process.
issue.usual_guard: A link or contract check, or a process rule.

design_flaw.means: It works as built, but the design fails a person or another part: a layout that breaks at one width, text too faint to read, a generator that writes its clone folder's name into shared files.
design_flaw.evidence: Screenshots at named widths and themes for anything visual; otherwise the input that shows the flaw.
design_flaw.usual_guard: A page check at the named widths and themes, or a test of the property.

annoyance.means: Nothing is broken, but it bothers a person who uses or owns it: vague wording, an old name that keeps coming back, a format they did not want. An annoyance is a real finding.
annoyance.evidence: The person's words, verbatim, with who said them, when, and where the annoying thing appears.
annoyance.usual_fix: Often a matter of taste: two or three options, and the person chooses through the taste palettes pack.
annoyance.usual_guard: A check that the old wording or format does not return, once the person has chosen.

telling_them_apart: Wrong behavior against a spec, a test or a promise: error.
Behavior as built, but the design fails someone or something: design_flaw.
Nothing wrong, but a person is bothered: annoyance.
Missing, stale, misconfigured, blocked or a mistake in a process: issue.
When two fit, pick the one whose fix you expect and say why; triage can change it.
value.security: Any kind can also be a security finding: set sensitivity to security when it could expose data, grant access or spend beyond a grant. It stays private and goes through the security review pack until its fix is in effect everywhere it was seen.

fingerprint_rule.component: The smallest named part where it was seen, in lowercase words joined by hyphens, without paths, line numbers, versions or dates.
fingerprint_rule.symptom: Two to six lowercase words joined by hyphens for what goes wrong, without names, ids or numbers that change.
fingerprint_rule.duplicates: Equal fingerprints are duplicates. The same kind and component with a different symptom is a judgment call, so triage says why it folded them together or kept them apart.

value.title: Severity guide: P0 to P3
value.category_reason: A scoring rubric that every finding is rated against.

P0.means: Harm is happening now: credentials or personal data exposed, money spent without authority, or a surface down for everyone.
P0.respond: Contain it first and stop other work.

P1.means: Wrong or missing results that people would rely on, or a path by which someone without the grant can read, write or spend.
P1.respond: Fix before building on the affected work.

P2.means: A real problem with a narrow trigger or a known workaround, a scope mistake only an already authorized caller can trigger, a process mistake that was caught and undone, or an annoyance the owner made a rule about.

P3.means: Cosmetic, stale or minor, with no wrong results: a layout problem at one width, a count out of date, a portability trap with a workaround.
P3.respond: Fix when nearby, or batch similar ones.

rules: Rate the impact on people and work, not the effort to fix.
The noticer sets a provisional level; triage confirms or changes it with a reason.
Never lower a level to make a finding look smaller. A tested workaround can lower it by one level, and the workaround is named.
A cause that keeps coming back can be raised by one level in a pattern review.
value.worked_examples_note: The worked examples are listed at the levels their noticers gave them.

value.title: Evidence checklist for each kind of finding
value.category_reason: Acceptance criteria that recording, reproduction and verification are checked against.
every_finding: What was seen, in one sentence; where; who noticed it; when, as a UTC date and time.
At least one piece of evidence a different worker could use to see the same problem.
Files, logs and screenshots stored by SHA-256, with credentials, personal data and private paths removed.
Anything not captured is marked unknown rather than guessed.

error: A minimal reproduction: the exact version or commit, the smallest input or command, and the expected and actual results.
Or a log excerpt with secrets removed, or a measurement with its method and sample size.
design_flaw: For anything visual: screenshots at named widths, by default 320, 768 and 1440 pixels, in every theme the surface offers, such as light and dark, with the page address and version.
For a flaw that is not visual: the input that shows it, such as the folder name or setting that triggers it.
annoyance: The person's words, verbatim, with who said them and when.
Where the annoying thing appears; two or three places are enough.
issue: The link, receipt, run id, status code or timestamp that shows it.
For a process issue: the direction that applied, where it was written, and the action that broke it, with times.

never: A credential value; say where it was, never what it was.
A screenshot or log that shows personal data or someone else's private information.
A claim of reproduction without a recorded run.

value.title: Disclosure rules for findings
value.category_reason: Guardrails that decide which findings may ever be described in public.
rules: Never publish details of an unfixed security finding. A security finding stays private until its fix is in effect everywhere the problem was seen; fixed_not_deployed is not enough.
Fixed findings, and findings with nothing sensitive in them, may be published once their owner agrees.
A finding marked public false stays private, even after it is fixed.
Never publish credentials, personal data, private names, private paths or private notes. Say where a secret was, never its value.
A public summary is a separate noun written for readers outside the team; the finding itself stays in the team's scope.
Publishing is the owner's act on a surface of their choice. No verb in this pack publishes anything.
Failures stay on the record in public too: a summary says plainly what went wrong, including mistakes in process.

deterministic_gate.check: The finding's public field is true.
A finding with sensitivity security has status fixed, verified or closed.
Sensitivity is none or security; credential, personal data and private context findings are never published.
The record checks' secret pattern finds nothing in the summary.
Every link is a public https address or a public pull request or commit reference.

deterministic_checks.why: Every finding is one of the four kinds, so triage and the evidence checklist apply.
Severity uses the guide's four levels.
Status uses the method's eight meanings.
The disclosure rules depend on sensitivity.
A finding shows what was seen.
Who noticed it is part of the record.
When it was noticed is part of the record.
Triage folds duplicates together by fingerprint.
An error comes with a reproduction, a log excerpt or a measurement.
A design flaw comes with screenshots, or for anything not visual the input that shows it.
An annoyance is recorded in the person's own words.
A finding marked fixed says what the fix is.
A fix is verified by a different worker than the one who made it.
A closed finding has a guard shown to fail without the fix, or a waiver.
A waiver says why no guard can run.
A duplicate points at the finding that keeps its evidence.
Only a person's recorded decision closes a finding as won't fix.

value.title: Worked example: a pattern review written by hand from the public findings
value.category_reason: An example output of review-patterns: hypotheses about shared causes, drawn from real findings.

patterns.cause: Acting on held or paused work before reading the newest owner direction
evidence: F-004: A pull request was merged after the owner asked to keep it unmerged; guard: process: read the newest owner handoff before merging.
F-005: A stopped evaluation was restarted against a 'do not restart' direction; guard: process: check the owner handoff before resuming paused work.
patterns.upstream_fix: One step before any merge, restart or resume: read the newest owner handoff first. Both findings' process guards name this step.
patterns.upstream: The single step both process guards describe, instead of one guard per action.
patterns.falsified_if: Another action against a written hold happens after that step is in place.

patterns.cause: One script copied into every repository, so one portability bug lives in every copy
evidence: F-006: The shared index generator writes the clone folder's name into generated files; pending: one portable version for the kit and every copy.
patterns.upstream_fix: One portable version for the kit and every copy, as F-006's pending propose-fix says.
patterns.upstream: The shared kit's copy of the script, which every repository copies.
patterns.falsified_if: A copy still writes its clone folder's name after the portable version lands.

patterns.cause: Retired names come back because each place checks for them its own way
evidence: F-011: Old pack brand names kept appearing in status messages, docs and pages; guard: retired-name tests in the home portal and the public noticeboard site.
F-019: The pack library's brand check spells the brand names in its own regex; fix in progress: store the names as hashes, as check_public.py does.
patterns.upstream_fix: One retired-name check that stores the names as hashes, as check_public.py does, reused by every repository and page.
patterns.upstream: A single shared name check instead of one per place.
patterns.falsified_if: A retired name reappears in a place that uses the shared check.
